capacity_gross_kwh.notes: ArenaEV Model 3 Standard: 69 kWh total (nominal), LFP. Sources conflict: Tesla does not disclose capacity; KBB shows N/A; Electra (France) gives about 64 kWh usable for the EU Standard. 2026 Standard (US).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Electra (France) states about 64 kWh usable for the Model 3 Standard (LFP, CATL); ArenaEV's 69 kWh total gives a plausible 93 % usable ratio. The French page covers the European Standard (US pack assumed the same). A Car and Driver figure of 69.5 kWh usable appeared only in a search excerpt (AOL), not opened. 2026 Standard (US).

chemistry.notes: LFP per ArenaEV and Electra (CATL). 2026 Standard (US).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: ArenaEV lists a 400 V system. 2026 Standard (US).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Tesla's release note (2020.24.6.4, Model S/3/X/Y) says the car preconditions its battery when navigating to a fast charger; this is a software feature delivered to the whole Model 3 line (2026 Standard (US).). Page mentions no manual battery-warming control. A manual control was neither found nor ruled out: Tesla's owner's manual pages were blocked (403) and scheduled-departure preconditioning in search excerpts is cabin-oriented.

dc_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs: 225 kW maximum input for the Standard (250 kW for the rest of the lineup); ArenaEV also 225 kW. Conflict: Electra (France) lists 175 kW and EU listings 170 kW for the European Standard. 2026 Standard (US).

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: ArenaEV lists 11 kW AC for the Model 3 Standard (European listing) and the existing OpenEV data for the 2026 Canadian Premium-I (same LFP RWD family) shows 11 kW. Older RWD cars were 7.6 kW (32 A, Wikipedia/Basenor, 2017-2023), so a lower North American single-phase limit is possible. 2026 Standard (US).
